Name: Cloudflare Workers
Runtime: V8 isolates with JavaScript and WebAssembly
Use Case: Request transformation and routing and APIs near users
Strengths: Streaming; service bindings; outbound TCP via cloudflare:sockets connect()
Weaknesses: CPU and memory and subrequest quotas depend on plan and trigger; outbound TCP has destination restrictions; no inbound TCP listener
Consistency Model: Compute has no durable state by itself; Workers KV is eventual; Durable Objects provide per-object strong consistency
Gotcha: Distinguish CPU from wall time: network waits do not consume CPU; configure paid CPU limits explicitly; do not use KV for atomic coordination

Name: Cloudflare Durable Objects
Runtime: Workers runtime with single-threaded execution per object
Use Case: Strongly consistent counters and sessions and coordination partitioned by object
Strengths: Private transactional strongly consistent storage; SQLite storage and point-in-time recovery; compute colocated with storage
Weaknesses: Hot objects limit throughput; placement affects latency; storage and CPU quotas depend on backend and plan
Consistency Model: Strong consistency and transactions within an object; no cross-object transaction boundary
Gotcha: Use SQLite-backed namespaces for new deployments; persist required state through Storage API because memory is lost on eviction or deployment; single active compute location does not mean non-durable storage

Name: Fastly Compute
Runtime: WebAssembly with WASI and Fastly-specific hostcalls
Use Case: Edge request processing and caching using compatible language SDKs
Strengths: Language SDKs; backend routing; cache control; Config Store and KV Store and Secret Store
Weaknesses: Arbitrary Wasm binaries are not automatically compatible; resource quotas and SDK support require deployment-specific checks
Consistency Model: Compute memory is not durable state; Fastly edge data stores are documented as durable and eventually consistent
Gotcha: Prefer supported SDKs and validate required hostcalls; VCL logic must be ported rather than run unchanged; VCL remains supported; do not assume WASI 0.3 availability from Wasm support alone

Name: AWS CloudFront Functions
Runtime: Restricted JavaScript runtime; runtime 2.0 required for KeyValueStore
Use Case: Viewer request and response rewriting and cache-key normalization and token validation
Strengths: Lightweight execution at CloudFront edge locations; KeyValueStore reads without arbitrary network access
Weaknesses: 10 KB function code limit versus 2 MB memory; no arbitrary network or file access or request body access
Consistency Model: Stateless execution; optional CloudFront KeyValueStore is separate distributed configuration
Gotcha: Use compute utilization metrics to budget execution; use Lambda@Edge when network or request body access is needed rather than assuming only header manipulation is possible

Name: AWS Lambda@Edge
Runtime: Supported Node.js or Python Lambda runtimes on x86_64
Use Case: CloudFront viewer and origin event processing requiring network or request body access
Strengths: Network access; third-party libraries; viewer and origin triggers
Weaknesses: Not full regional Lambda: no VPC attachment or layers or custom environment variables or container images or provisioned concurrency; event-specific quotas
Consistency Model: Execution is not a durable data store; external state consistency depends on the chosen service and configuration
Gotcha: Publish a numbered function version in us-east-1; aliases and $LATEST are unsupported; use currently supported runtimes and account for request body truncation

Name: Vercel Edge Functions
Runtime: Vercel Functions using the V8-based Edge runtime; JavaScript/TypeScript
Use Case: Existing Edge-runtime workloads with compatible frameworks and dependencies
Strengths: Web APIs; streaming; preferred regions; automatic regional failover
Weaknesses: Subset of Node.js APIs; no filesystem access; bundle limits vary by plan; framework support must be checked
Consistency Model: Runtime provides no durable state guarantee; consistency belongs to the external data store and is not implied by a paid plan
Gotcha: Historical row name retained; Vercel recommends migrating Edge runtime workloads to Node.js; docs say Next.js 16.3 no longer supports runtime=edge for routes and pages; 25 seconds to start a response is not a 25ms CPU quota

Name: Edge KV Stores
Runtime: Provider-specific; Workers KV as documented example
Use Case: Read-heavy configuration and feature flags with acceptable staleness
Strengths: Globally cached reads; simple key-value API; useful for infrequent writes
Weaknesses: Cold reads may reach central storage; cached misses also delay visibility; quotas and guarantees vary by provider
Consistency Model: Workers KV is eventually consistent; updates may take 60 seconds or more elsewhere; even local immediate visibility is not guaranteed
Gotcha: Do not use Workers KV for atomic counters or inventory or immediate revocation; serializing writes through a Durable Object does not make downstream KV reads strongly consistent

Name: WASI (WebAssembly System Interface)
Runtime: WebAssembly modules or components with versioned host interfaces
Use Case: Sandboxed portable components where the target runtime implements the required WASI interfaces
Strengths: Capability-based access; cross-language component composition; WASI 0.3 native async
Weaknesses: Runtime and language tooling support differ; provider-specific hostcalls reduce portability; not all proposals are stable
Consistency Model: N/A - interface specifications rather than a data store
Gotcha: Official releases list WASI 0.3 as stable and current; 0.2 is stable but superseded; 0.1 is legacy; pin compatible WIT and toolchain versions and verify host support before migration

Name: Edge Databases
Runtime: Provider-specific SQL services; Turso libSQL embedded replicas as one example
Use Case: Read-heavy SQL near applications with explicit write and synchronization semantics
Strengths: Embedded replicas serve local reads; Turso supports production embedded replicas and recommends Turso Sync for new sync projects
Weaknesses: Embedded replicas need a filesystem; other-replica reads lag synchronization; offline writes require explicit support and configuration
Consistency Model: Not universally eventual or multi-writer: Turso embedded replicas default to primary writes and read-your-writes on the initiating replica; other replicas require sync
Gotcha: Do not infer conflict resolution or offline writes from the edge label; distinguish libSQL embedded replicas from Turso Database with Turso Sync; verify runtime storage and SDK semantics before deployment

Name: CDN as Compute Platform
Runtime: Provider-specific edge runtimes with placement controls
Use Case: Request routing and authentication near users with backend-heavy work placed near data
Strengths: Can reduce origin traffic and request latency when compute placement matches dependencies
Weaknesses: Repeated cross-region database calls can erase edge latency gains; placement controls have handler-specific restrictions
Consistency Model: Compute location does not define consistency; selected database and cache contracts do
Gotcha: Measure end-to-end request duration; consider backend-near placement for chatty data access; Cloudflare placement documentation limits placement to fetch handlers rather than assuming RPC entrypoints are relocated

Name: Cloudflare D1 Read Replication
Runtime: SQLite-based D1 with Workers binding Sessions API
Use Case: Scale geographically distributed SQL reads while preserving session ordering
Strengths: Managed read replicas; bookmarks preserve read-your-writes and monotonic reads across requests
Weaknesses: All writes go to the primary; replica lag can add waiting; Sessions API is unavailable via REST API
Consistency Model: Asynchronous replication with sequential consistency within Sessions API sessions; not universal latest-data reads
Gotcha: Enable read replication and use withSession or queries stay on primary; carry bookmarks across requests; use first-primary when the initial query needs latest data; unconstrained sessions may start stale

Name: Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore
Use Case: Redirect maps and feature flags updated independently of function code
Strengths: Global configuration reads from Functions without arbitrary network access; separate data update API
Weaknesses: Function helper methods are read-only; deployment quotas apply; propagation is not instantaneous
Consistency Model: Values do not change during an invocation; updates are applied between invocations; no global immediate visibility guarantee
Gotcha: Associate the store before use; handle missing-key errors; use the KeyValueStore API ETag for writes rather than the different CloudFront API ETag; meta lastUpdatedDateTime excludes edge propagation time

Name: Cloudflare Workers Cache API
Use Case: Explicit caching of reusable HTTP responses within a data center
Strengths: Programmatic cache keys and expiration; conditional reads with ETag and Last-Modified
Weaknesses: Contents are not replicated outside the originating data center; cache.put does not support tiered caching; misses require application handling
Consistency Model: Local response cache rather than durable storage or globally coherent state; cache.delete purges only the current data center
Gotcha: Use fetch-based caching when tiered caching is needed; implement miss and expiration handling; do not treat a local delete as global invalidation or strip privacy protections merely to force caching
